summary: Modular monolith: React Native (Expo), Java + Spring Boot, PostgreSQL (managed or self-hosted) database on AWS ECS on Fargate. It keeps data in Indian regions, matches the team's languages and is estimated at $3,600-$6,900 per month.

frontend.justification: React Native (Expo) matches the team's typescript skills; covers android and ios and web from one codebase; depends on native module quality; is a proven choice for fintech projects.

alternatives.why_not: Flutter scores 1.1 points lower overall, mainly on team skill fit (1.1 points).

backend.justification: Java + Spring Boot matches the team's java/kotlin skills; has mature security defaults for handling payments; Spring Security, long audit history; is a proven choice for fintech projects.

alternatives.why_not: Node.js + NestJS scores 0.8 points lower overall, mainly on security (1.0 points) and performance (0.5 points).
C# + ASP.NET Core scores 1.4 points lower overall, mainly on team skill fit (1.1 points) and compatibility with the rest of the stack (0.6 points).

database.justification: PostgreSQL (managed or self-hosted) gives ACID transactions for money-handling data; can be placed in Mumbai (ap-south-1) to keep data in India; carries PCI DSS attestation; has headroom for the expected load.

alternatives.why_not: Microsoft SQL Server / Azure SQL is a close second: only 1.2 points behind, with no single weakness.
CockroachDB scores 1.7 points lower overall, mainly on compatibility with the rest of the stack (0.5 points).

tradeoffs: Write scaling beyond one primary needs design

hosting.justification: AWS ECS on Fargate runs on AWS as preferred; can be placed in Mumbai (ap-south-1) to keep data in India; offers a 99.99% SLA, in line with the 99.95% target; IAM roles, VPC isolation.

alternatives.why_not: AWS EKS (Kubernetes) is a close second: only 0.1 points behind, with no single weakness.
AWS EC2 (self-managed VMs) scores 1.1 points lower overall, mainly on security (0.5 points) and maintainability (0.5 points).

assumptions: Load estimate: peak about 1K requests/second and about 108M requests/month from 300K users in 12 months.
Usage-priced items are shown as a band (0.75x to 1.3x of the estimate) because load figures are order-of-magnitude.
Public list prices of each product, in USD, without taxes, committed-use discounts or developer time.
The 99.95% availability target doubles or adds redundancy for hosting and database where needed.
Cache (Managed Redis/Valkey (ElastiCache, Memorystore, Azure Cache)): about $81-$190/month
ML (Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint (small instance)): about $150-$440/month

warnings.message: Use a hosted checkout or tokenisation from a PCI DSS Level 1 provider so card numbers never touch your servers; otherwise the whole stack is in PCI scope.

ISO 27001 audits your own controls (access reviews, change management, logging, incident response); vendors with their own ISO 27001 report shorten the audit, and gaps in the chosen stack are listed separately.
SMS to Indian numbers needs DLT registration (entity, sender ID and message templates) with a telecom operator before launch; allow one to two weeks.
DPDP Act: record consent, support erasure and correction, notify breaches, and take extra care with children's data. Cross-border transfer is allowed except to countries the government restricts.
RBI localisation: payment data must be stored only in India, so database, backups and logs are kept in Indian regions.

Expected cost ($3,600-$6,900) is inside the $6,000 budget at typical load but can pass it at peak usage; watch hosting (AWS ECS on Fargate, $1,600-$2,800) and database (PostgreSQL (managed or self-hosted), $930-$1,700) first.
Razorpay: use Standard Checkout or hosted fields so card numbers are tokenised by Razorpay and never touch your servers; this keeps you in the lightest PCI DSS scope.
ISO 27001 is required, but Expo Push Notifications lists no ISO 27001 attestation in the knowledge base; ask the vendor for evidence (DPA, audit report) or replace it.

assumptions: No extra inputs supplied; neutral defaults are used (learning appetite medium, lock-in tolerance medium, budget strictness firm, no hiring plan, no mobile preference).
Auth: Amazon Cognito replaced by Keycloak to bring the stack toward the budget (about $2,600 per month cheaper).

pipeline: filter each layer by hard constraints

robustness.summary: The same stack wins in 7 of 14 checks. It switches to AWS EKS (Kubernetes) (hosting) when cost counted half as much, time to market counted half as much, scalability counted twice as much, performance counted twice as much, maintainability counted half as much, security counted twice as much; and to Node.js + NestJS (backend), AWS Lambda + API Gateway (hosting) when budget halved ($3,000).

Gives up 2.1 points, mainly on vendor lock-in (-1.1 pts), security (-1.0 pts), performance (-1.0 pts).
